one_liner: Senior supervisor at DFC leading a team that screens overseas investment projects for environmental and social risks, setting policy and briefing leadership and outside stakeholders.
fit_summary: This GS-15 role requires one year of GS-14-equivalent experience overseeing environmental and social (E&S) risk management across many projects, building E&S policy, and supervising a team. Daniel's emergency-management consulting at IEM and policy and people skills help with stakeholder engagement, but nothing on file shows E&S due diligence or supervisory experience at that level. Unless Daniel's IEM work involved leading environmental or social risk reviews and managing staff, this is unlikely to clear the qualifications screen.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); a parallel Merit Promotion announcement (27-ODP-ST-13098029-BN) exists for status candidates, but Daniel without federal status should use this public one.

One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14 covering ALL four areas: overseeing E&S risk management across a wide range of projects, briefing leadership or external stakeholders on E&S analysis, collaborating on E&S policies and methodologies, and supervising a team.
Education cannot substitute at GS-15; experience alone counts, though volunteer experience is credited.
Secret security clearance required (obtainable after selection, but expect a background investigation).
All requirements must be met by the closing date, November 5, 2026.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work covered all four specialized-experience elements; if it lacks E&S risk oversight or supervision, consider lower-graded emergency management, FEMA, or policy roles instead.

If you did assess project risks, such as hazard mitigation, environmental and historic preservation (EHP) reviews, or social and community impacts in disaster recovery, describe that work using the posting's E&S language. Only claim it if it is accurate.
Address each of the four required elements explicitly within your two-page resume. List start and end dates (month/year) and hours per week for each job, and state any team size you supervised.
Preview the questionnaire at apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13098028 and answer conservatively. Every 'expert' rating must be backed by your resume, because overstating can get you removed.
The window is only October 28 to November 5, 2026, so prepare your resume in advance and submit several days early.
resume_bullets: Supervised a team of [number] [titles] reviewing [number] [type of projects] for [environmental/social/hazard] risks, ensuring compliance with [specific standards, e.g., FEMA EHP, NEPA, IFC Performance Standards].
Briefed [client agency leadership/external stakeholders] on [risk assessment findings/policy recommendations] for [program], leading to [actual decision or outcome].
Collaborated with [teams/agencies] to develop and disseminate [new/revised procedure or methodology] for [risk management process], adopted by [who/how many users].
interview_questions: Describe how you led a team through a complex risk assessment of a project with significant environmental or social concerns.
Tell us about a time you briefed senior leadership or external stakeholders on a sensitive, contested issue. How did you handle pushback?
How have you developed or improved a risk management policy or methodology and ensured consistent implementation across a team?
How do you hold team members accountable while supporting their professional development?
watch_outs: The required specialized experience is narrow and highly technical (E&S due diligence at a GS-15 level), and Daniel's known background does not clearly match it.
Supervisory experience is mandatory; without documented people-management experience you will not qualify.
Requires a Secret clearance. The application window is short (closes Nov 5, 2026), and the role is in-office in DC with telework, so expect a commute from Manassas.
